messages.subject: NBLAST search with FAFB (EM) neurons
messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues,

I just wanted to point out a fairly recent feature of the online NBLAST server hosted by virtual fly brain at

  https://nblast.virtualflybrain.org:8080/NBLAST_on-the-fly/

that may be of interest to some. This now supports the FAFB14 template brain, meaning that you can search EM reconstructions against FlyCircuit single neurons. I provide a brief walkthrough below. Note that the incoming SWC file must be calibrated in nm (and not microns) like the FAFB14 brain.

Best,

Greg.

0. Sample neuron https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/?pid=1&zp=120960&yp=199684&xp=487219&tool=tracingtool&active_skeleton_id=27295&active_node_id=2016950&sid0=1&s0=0&help=true
1. Download SWC file from CATMAID using the Export Widget (Use Control+Space to find it)
2. Upload to NBLAST search tool. You may need to choose the mirror option. Make sure you pick the FAFB14 template brain.

messages.subject_clean: visualizing an nrrd average brain image in nat with im3d
messages.body_plain:
Hello Mr Jefferis!

I have a quick follow up from our past discussion and was hoping you could point me to some resources/functions that might help me with importing an average brain image into R. So far, I have been able to transform and import all the neuron swc files perfectly and can view them in the bounding box of the average.nrrd brain file that I import using as.templatebrain and plot3d. However, like I said before, the template brain that is constructed from the .nrrd does not seem to have the surface information necessary to plot the brain as an object rather than simply a boundary box.

(when I try to do this, I get an error that says...
Error in get(paste0(as.character(x), ".surf")) :
  object 'average.surf' not found)

To try and fix this, I was able to import a .stl file out of Imaris (which I am using instead of Amira) and thought that I might be able to plot this instead since it is closer to the mesh object that Amira supports (hxsurf). This does not seem to work either though and I have been stuck for some time. Do you happen to know of the best way to get a 3d representation of an average brain in R given a .nrrd file and a .stl file. Any advice or pointers would be very much appreciated!

Thanks,

Max

> Hello!
>
> I have been working for a while on registering zebrafish telencephalon brain images and creating an average from those registrations using cmtk on the command line. Now I am at a point where I have generated and average .nrrd file and have registered each original brain to that average so that I can begin warping the neuron objects accordingly. Using nat package, I have been able to import the swc neuron files (which I exported from Imaris) and transform them by the registration .list files. However, what I am unsure about is how to import the average brain image so I can plot a 3d representation of the surface and then graph the neurons on top of that. Is this what I should be using im3d for or is there a better way to visualize the average brain image and neurons on a 3d plot? I do not have access to Amira and when I import the transformed swc files back into Imaris they are always outside of the boundaries of the average image files so I am unsure of how to proceed.
>
> Thanks!
>
> Max

messages.subject: Viewing sub-volume connectivity
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a set of neuron skeletons that I've managed to import as a neuronlist as well as a neuropil volume that I've imported as hxsurf. The neurons were already registered to the neuropil volume and both were exported directly from Amira. My goal now is to do the same analysis that was done in the Fretcher et al. 2019 paper of the lateral horn (https://elifesciences.org/articles/44590) as well as in the recent natverse paper (supplementary figure 4a). I want to try and extract meaningful subvolume information that is based on the projection areas of the neurons that innervate this neuropil.

I'm new to both natverse and R, so I've some difficulty getting this to work. My main question is this: how do I actually integrate these two data objects (i.e. the neuronlist and the hxsurf)? I've been able to use nblast_all-by-all and nhclust to generate a cluster dendrogram of the neuronlist, but this is about as far as I've gotten.

Thanks for any advice!
Kind regards,
Marcel

messages.body_plain:
Hi Marcel,

do you want to look for neurons inside a mesh or define a sub volume based on neuronal projection patterns.

The workhorse function for dealing with neurons inside a mesh is pointsinside. It's listed as one of the functions for working with meshes here.

http://natverse.org/nat/reference/index.html#section-surfaces-and-landmarks-hxsurf-mesh-d-

If you want to define subvolumes based on neuronal projection patterns, I think Alex cced can point you to some code online that he used for those figures.

All the best,

Greg.

messages.subject_clean: Importing data to use in NBLAST
messages.body_plain:
Hello again Dr. Jefferis!

Thanks to all your previous help and guidance, I am currently in the process of comparing neurons generated from data that I have collected form around 50 zebrafish. So far, I have been importing the neurons as swc files and would now like to not only compare them (using NBLAST) amongst each other, but also compare them to neurons from other datasets besides my own. While these datasets are not online like your fly database, I do have access to the .swc files and was considering importing these files into RStudio as well and then converting to dotprops like before to run NBLAST functions. However, there are many more neurons in this dataset and I am worried that importing the 1000s of neurons in this dataset as swc files on my local desktop computer might not be very efficient. Do you think this is the best way to go about running NBLAST using two large datasets of neurons or is there another way/resource that I should use to to do this?

Thanks,

Max

messages.subject: Re: Importing data to use in NBLAST
messages.subject_clean: Importing data to use in NBLAST
messages.body_plain:
Dear Max,

> Thanks to all your previous help and guidance, I am currently in the process of comparing neurons generated from data that I have collected form around 50 zebrafish. So far, I have been importing the neurons as swc files and would now like to not only compare them (using NBLAST) amongst each other, but also compare them to neurons from other datasets besides my own. While these datasets are not online like your fly database, I do have access to the .swc files and was considering importing these files into RStudio as well and then converting to dotprops like before to run NBLAST functions. However, there are many more neurons in this dataset and I am worried that importing the 1000s of neurons in this dataset as swc files on my local desktop computer might not be very efficient. Do you think this is the best way to go about running NBLAST using two large datasets of neurons or is there another way/resource that I should use to to do this?

There is no problem with importing this many neurons. We routinely search a single neuron against thousands of neurons. You should just to something like:

nl=read.neurons('/path/to/swcs')
# this implies 1 micron step size
# the divide by 1.0 could be changed to e.g. 2.0 to make the size of your neurons more "fly-like"
dps=dotprops(nl/1.0, k=5, resample=1)
sc=nblast(myneuron, nl, .progress='text', normalised=T)
top10sc=sort(sc, decreasing=TRUE)[1:10]
# plot top 10 hits
plot3d(names(top10sc), db=nl)

You can also do nblast_allbyall <http://natverse.org/nat.nblast/reference/nblast_allbyall.html> with that many neurons. something like:

myneurons = read.neurons("path1")
theirneurons = read.neurons("path2")
allneurons=c(myneurons, theirneurons)
all.aba=nblast_allbyall(allneurons)
all.hc=nhclust(scoremat=all.aba)

see http://natverse.org/nat.nblast/reference/nblast_allbyall.html http://natverse.org/nat.nblast/articles/NBLAST-Clustering.html.

Finally I would note that the fishatlas <https://natverse.github.io/fishatlas/> package allows downloads of the Kunst and Baier dataset directly.

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] .obj files for FAFB_v14 neuropil
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dudi,

You can use

https://rdrr.io/rforge/rgl/man/writeOBJ.html

to write out obj files but first you need to convert to mesh3d format. In one line:

library(natverse)
writeOBJ(as.mesh3d(FAFB.surf), “FAFB.obj”)

To convert all the individual neuropil domains, you must first convert them each to mesh3d

for(n in FAFB14NP.surf$RegionList) {
writeOBJ(as.mesh3d(subset(FAFB14NP.surf,n)), paste0(n,“FAFB.obj”)
}

(Unchecked from my phone, you’ll need to fix the smart quotes, maybe you can repost corrected).

All the best,

Greg.

Dear Dudi,

Thanks for posting back. I would actually still recommend what I wrote in my second post:

> Rvcg::vcgObjWrite(as.mesh3d(FAFB.surf), "FAFB.obj")
> for(n in FAFB14NP.surf$RegionList) {
>   Rvcg::vcgObjWrite(as.mesh3d(subset(FAFB14NP.surf,n)), paste0(n,".obj"))
> }

This uses the Rvcg package (which is installed by default with the natverse and is available on the standard CRAN package repository) to write the mesh (see https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/Rvcg/versions/0.18/topics/vcgObjWrite).

This has two advantages.

1. The important one is that It avoids duplicate vertices in the mesh – rgl::writeOBJ generates files based on the current rgl 3D display but this does not retain the full connectivity information of the mesh.
2. It also avoids generating 76 3D windows! Replaces open3d with clear3d to avoid that.

All the best,

Greg.
